Observations:
The soil water content of pots was maintained close to 85 % of water holding capacity by replenishing in the evening 100 % of the daily water loss determined by weighing. Values were retrieved by digitalizing Fig. 4 and 5 with WebPlot Digitizer.
Those figure show diurnal variation, and I picked the values at 12 :00, which corresponds to the time of the day with the most negative leaf water potential.

I put NA to standard errors which I was not able to distinguish from the point. Total tree leaf area was estimated but not provided in any wyas in the manuscript.

Reference_title: Effect of vapor pressure deficit on the photosynthesis, growth, and nutrient absorption of tomato seedlings
Observations: 1 plant per pot: this is why I put 1 in setm density but unsure this was suited to this column. pots were weighed and watered every day to maintain the substrate water content at 85-90% field capacity. Soil in the pot is a mix of perlite and vermiculite at a 2:1 volume ratio. All values and corresponding standard errors (Kplant, gs, E, leaf water potential) were digitized using WebPlotDigitizer on Fig. 1a, 1c, 2a and 2c. One value per variety and treatment (low or high VPD)  four values, each corresponding to the average across five seedlings. Leaf area and height come from Table 2.

Reference_title: Responses of sap flux and stomatal conductance of Pinus taeda L. trees to stepwise reductions in leaf area
Observations: 10 trees progressively defoliated/harvested by canopy layer from the bottom up, finishing with stem harvest, all within one day. 2 reference trees not defoliated. BA extracted from Fig 7 (average BA increment / yr * age) for 10 trees. LAI measured both by Li-COR LAI 2000 plant canopy analyser (all 12 trees) and destructive method (10 trees). Average total LA of 10 trees prior to any destruction reported on Fig 5 (note, this is different the number I can come up with by integrating the dry mass in Fig 1 and multiplying the SLA by it). SWP not measured but assumed to be 0 due to well-watered conditions. SF is not extractable as it doesn't appear in a timeseries. Kwp extracted from Fig 7 for all 12 trees (it is reported as a whole-tree conductance but directly calculated from sapwood-specific sap flux density so I categorised it as being at the sapwood level).
